scenes.title: The picture (Scene 1)
scenes.vo: Picture a train. Identical cars, permanently coupled, sitting on one straight length of track. That picture is what an array actually is.

scenes.title: The definition (Scene 2)
scenes.vo: One contiguous block of memory. Equal-sized slots, packed end to end. So you never walk the platform counting cars. You compute.

scenes.title: Why indexing is O(1) (Scene 3)
scenes.vo: The address of slot i is the base address plus i times the slot size. One multiply. One add. That cost does not grow with the array. That is what O of one means.

scenes.title: The contrast (Scene 4)
scenes.vo: Reaching item seven in a linked chain means seven hops. Here, seven is a number you multiply. No other position is touched.

scenes.title: Where the train breaks (Scene 5)
scenes.vo: Now the limit. The track behind the caboose already belongs to something else. A raw array cannot grow in place, for exactly that reason.

scenes.title: Doubling (Scene 6)
scenes.vo: So a dynamic array builds a longer train on fresh track and moves every car across. Double the capacity each time, and the copying across n appends sums to under two n. Constant work per append, amortized.

scenes.title: In place (Scene 7)
scenes.vo: The rest of the module stays inside one array. A read pointer and a write pointer. Write never passes read, so you can never destroy a value you still need.

scenes.title: Close (Scene 8)
scenes.vo: Four concept lessons, five problems, one practice set. Module four of the leetExpert DSA course. Free in early access at leetexpert dot com.
